title: How the day ended
text: Stocks rose on Wednesday. The S&P 500 fund SPY gained 1.7% to $766.81 and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ gained 1.0% to $691.95. Big AI companies did well: Microsoft rose 6.7%, Amazon 6.1% and Alphabet 3.2%. Companies that supply the AI boom had a harder day: Vertiv fell 12.9%, NVIDIA 3.2% and TSMC 2.4%. Tomorrow, watch whether the big companies keep their gains. One strong day does not make a trend.

title: Big AI companies rose, chip and equipment makers fell
text: Microsoft closed at $555.80, just under its 52 week high of $559.15. Amazon gained 6.1% and Alphabet 3.2%. In the other group, NVIDIA lost 3.2%, TSMC 2.4% and Broadcom 2.0%. We could not confirm one reason for these moves, so we only report the numbers. Comparing these two groups helps you see that companies tied to the same trend do not always move together.

title: Vertiv dropped almost 13% in one day
text: Vertiv, which makes power and cooling equipment for data centers, closed at $205.58, down 12.9%. On October 28 the company reported sales up 61% and raised its yearly outlook, according to its filing summary, so today's drop is a good example of a stock falling after good news. We could not confirm the cause of today's move. A drop this big is a reminder of how risky single stocks can be.

title: Lockheed Martin fell 7%
text: Lockheed Martin, a defense company, closed at $594.57, down 7.0%. It is usually a calmer stock, with a beta of only 0.1. Beta measures how much a stock tends to swing compared with the whole market. We could not confirm why it fell today, so no cause is given here. Even steady companies can have sharp days.

title: Government bond rates are at a 12 month high
text: The 10 year Treasury yield is the interest rate the U.S. government pays to borrow for ten years. Its monthly average rose to 5.13% in October, up from 4.06% a year earlier. When safe bonds pay more, some investors may prefer them over stocks, so this number is worth watching.

title: Lesson 37: Why can a stock fall on good news?
text: A stock price is not only about how a company did. It is also about what people expected. Imagine you hoped for an A on a test and got a B plus. The grade is good, but you feel let down. Investors feel the same way. If a company reports strong results but investors hoped for even more, the price can drop. The reverse can happen too: a company with weak results can rise if people feared something worse. This is why smart investors ask two questions: how did the company do, and how did that compare with what everyone expected?

title: What this update covers
text: Prices come from the market close on November 4. Analyst targets and ratios are available for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE only. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical have price data but no analyst targets or ratios. Reasons for several price moves could not be verified. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell.
